results.title: Stocks to Watch as the Fed Raises Interest Rates
results.body: Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia and RHB Sekuritas Indonesia recommend focusing on BBCA, BBRI, ELSA, MYOR, MDKA, MIKA, SMSM, LSIP and EXCL, citing consensus 12‑month target prices of Rp8,154, Rp3,851, Rp1,103, Rp2,483, Rp3,961, Rp2,715, Rp2,250, Rp1,933 and Rp3,267 respectively as of 21 September 2026, and noting that a majority of analysts rate BBCA and BBRI as buys. These recommendations follow the Federal Reserve’s 25‑basis‑point rate hike to a 3.75‑4 % target range last week, which is expected to tighten global monetary policy and increase funding costs for Indonesian equities.

results.title: Rising Wheat Prices Pressure Margins of ICBP, INDF, MYOR and Other Consumer Goods Emitters
results.body: The article reports that the sharp rise in global wheat prices to US$766 per bushel, a 52.5% year‑on‑year increase, is expected to weigh on the margins of Indonesian consumer‑goods issuers. Analysts at Mirae Asset note that ICBP (a subsidiary of INDF), INDF (parent of ICBP) and MYOR have seen quarterly gross‑profit‑margin (GPM) declines of 4.8, 4.3 and 2.2 percentage points respectively in 2022, and project that a 5% rise in flour prices could cut 2026 GPM by 0.5‑0.6 points and net profit by up to 3.6% for these firms. Kiwoom highlights that ROTI, ICBP, STTP, INDF and MYOR are the most exposed, with wheat accounting for 15% of ICBP’s COGS, 10% of MYOR’s and 9% of INDF’s, while each company holds roughly three months of wheat inventory. The report maintains a neutral recommendation for the consumer sector, while giving MYOR a buy‑trade target of Rp 1,720‑1,750, noting that margin pressure may intensify from Q4‑2026 to Q1‑2027.

results.title: Foreign investors lead net buying in BBRI, BBCA and BMRI, with the ten largest net‑buy stocks on Friday (21/8)
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors recorded the largest net purchases in Indonesian stocks on Friday, 21 August 2026, with PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) leading the list. BBRI attracted a net buy of Rp 628.49 billion, followed by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp 269.09 billion and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with Rp 140.01 billion. The remaining top‑ten net‑buy stocks were PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) Rp 137.30 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) Rp 113.14 billion, PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) Rp 99.03 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) Rp 27.61 billion, PT Timah Tbk (TINS) Rp 26.91 billion, PT Mayora Indah Tbk (MYOR) Rp 17.08 billion and PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk (NSSS) Rp 15.78 billion. The total foreign net buying across the market amounted to Rp 974.57 billion, while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,525.69, up 0.37% (24.10 points). The article also notes sectoral gains, with the IDX Infrastructure sector up 0.47% and IDX Financial up 0.32%, providing context for the buying activity.

results.title: RANS Entertainment Indonesia Discloses IPO Proceeds Allocation, Emphasizing Debt Repayment
results.body: RANS Entertainment Indonesia Tbk announced how the Rp429.25 billion raised in its recent IPO will be allocated, with debt repayment being the first priority. Approximately Rp29.95 billion (6.98% of proceeds) will be used to settle existing credit facilities, while the remaining funds are earmarked for concerts (Rp161.5 billion, 37.61%), the acquisition of a 51 % stake in PT Rans Kosmetika Indonesia (Rp85 billion, 19.80%), development of the Cipungland entertainment park (Rp80 billion, 18.64%), an AI joint‑venture with PT Feedloop Global Teknologi (Rp35 billion, 8.15%) and working‑capital support for PT Rans Nikmat Sejahtera (Rp37.8 billion). The company also confirmed a strategic partnership with PT Mayora Indah Tbk to co‑develop intellectual‑property assets across live entertainment, music and family experiences. The disclosure aligns with the prospectus and was presented by President Director Nagita Slavina on 11 August 2026.

results.title: PT Mayora Indah Tbk reports modest net profit rise and 315.8% surge in operating cash flow
results.body: PT Mayora Indah Tbk, the snack food and beverage issuer, posted H1‑2026 net profit of Rp1.70 trillion, a slight increase from Rp1.66 trillion a year earlier. Operating cash flow jumped 315.8% to Rp4.02 trillion, supported by cash receipts from customers of Rp19.78 trillion, up 5.3% YoY. The company’s gross profit rose to Rp4.61 trillion, cost of goods sold fell to Rp13.30 trillion, and cash and cash equivalents grew to Rp5.60 trillion despite a reduction in total assets. Shares traded around Rp1,710 intraday, reflecting a year‑to‑date decline of about 19.7%.

results.title: IHSG Opens Higher Thanks to Destry Damayanti’s Nomination as BI Governor
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) opened on Tuesday, 11 August 2026 at 6,383 points, up 18.43 points (0.29%) as the nomination of Destry Damayanti as the sole candidate for Bank Indonesia governor boosted market sentiment and the rupiah to Rp17,755 per US$. Trading saw 4.36 billion shares exchanged for Rp1.31 trillion, with 160 stocks gaining, 328 losing and 202 unchanged, while brokers highlighted technical support around 6,300–6,320 and resistance near 6,400–6,450. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommended PSAB, ESSA and BWPT; Phintraco Sekuritas listed HRUM, ESSA, ADRO, AADI and MYOR; CGS International pointed to HRUM, MYOR, BFIN, BBTN, EMAS and MDKA; and Panin Sekuritas favored MDKA, BBTN and INKP for the session. The outlook was tempered by upcoming retail‑sales data projected to improve to 1.8% YoY and US inflation releases, which could influence further index movement.

results.title: CGS International Sekuritas reports only 18% of covered issuers missed H1 2026 earnings targets and revises its top‑pick list
results.body: CGS International Sekuritas said only 18% of its 40 covered issuers fell short of earnings expectations in the first half of 2026, the lowest share in three years. Net profit growth for the covered group accelerated from 3% year‑on‑year in Q1 to 26% year‑on‑year in Q2, driven by agriculture, oil & gas, technology (GOTO) and retail (MAPA). Banking profit growth rose from 11% to 14% YoY and consumer‑goods profit growth from 10% to 25% YoY, while CGS removed MYOR, BMRI and KLBF from its top‑pick list and added BFIN, UNVR and JPFA, keeping BBCA, BBNI, ASII, UNVR, EXCL, TINS, JPFA, MAPA, BFIN and WIIM as its current selections. Since their inclusion, MYOR fell 4%, BMRI 2% and KLBF rose 3%; CGS cautions that August’s FTSE index update, the 2027 budget draft and a new Bank Indonesia governor could affect market volatility.

results.title: Maybank Sekuritas maintains buy on PT Mayora Indah Tbk with target Rp 2,500, citing consumer‑sector safe‑haven benefits as rupiah weakens to Rp 18,000 per USD
results.body: Maybank Sekuritas analyst Willy Goutama continues to recommend a buy on PT Mayora Indah Tbk, labeling it a consumer‑sector safe haven as the rupiah trades around Rp 18,000 per USD. He keeps the target price at Rp 2,500 per share, based on a 2026 price‑to‑earnings multiple of 17.9× and projected 2026 revenue of Rp 41.65 trillion with net profit of Rp 3.13 trillion. Recent results show Q1 2026 core profit of Rp 1.5 trillion (+38% YoY, excluding a Rp 309 billion currency gain) and a gross margin of 25.7%, up 450 basis points year‑on‑year, while Q2 2026 core profit rose 24% YoY to Rp 603 billion with a 7% sales increase. The firm also notes Mayora’s shift to net‑cash status, an EPS compound annual growth rate of 15.4% for 2025‑2028, and an expected dividend yield of 3.3‑4.4%, while warning that slower sales growth could pose a risk.

results.title: Mayora Indah Tbk reports net profit of Rp1.70 trillion, up 46.5% in H1 2026
results.body: PT Mayora Indah Tbk posted a net profit of Rp1.70 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 46.5% increase year‑over‑year. Revenue rose modestly to Rp17.92 trillion and basic earnings per share climbed to Rp77 from Rp52. The company’s food‑packaging segment generated Rp11.21 trillion in sales, while beverage sales reached Rp8.09 trillion; domestic sales fell 0.2% to Rp10.41 trillion, but sales in Asia and outside Asia grew 1.5% and 7.9% respectively. Total assets declined to Rp28.52 trillion, liabilities fell to Rp10.07 trillion and equity rose to Rp18.44 trillion, aided by a 5.1% reduction in cost of goods sold.

results.title: PT Mayora Indah Tbk reports 46.52% increase in H1 2026 net profit to Rp1.70 trillion
results.body: PT Mayora Indah Tbk., the listed producer of Kopiko, posted a net profit of Rp1.70 trillion for the January–June 2026 period, a 46.52% year‑on‑year increase. Revenue grew modestly 0.70% YoY to Rp17.92 trillion, with food‑in‑packaging sales of Rp11.21 trillion and beverage sales of Rp8.09 trillion. The company reduced cost of goods sold by 5.06% to Rp13.30 trillion, supporting the profit surge, while total assets fell to Rp28.52 trillion and liabilities to Rp10.07 trillion, lifting equity to Rp18.44 trillion.

results.title: Rupiah Weakening Pressures PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk, PT Mayora Indah Tbk, PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk, and PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk as Analysts Adjust Recommendations
results.body: The article examines how the rupiah’s slide above IDR 18,000 per US $ is pressuring PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk, PT Mayora Indah Tbk, PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk and PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk. PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk is most exposed because most of its brands are imported, while the other three also face higher input costs but benefit from strong cash, hedging and pricing power. First‑half‑2026 results show PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk revenue Rp 24.16 trillion (+23.36% YoY) and profit Rp 1.21 trillion (+26.49% YoY); PT Mayora Indah Tbk sales Rp 17.92 trillion (+0.7% YoY) and profit Rp 1.71 trillion (+46.53% YoY); PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk sales Rp 41.86 trillion (+11% YoY) with profit Rp 3.7 trillion (‑33% YoY); PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk sales Rp 16.89 trillion (+7.05% YoY) and profit Rp 2.97 trillion (+37.7% YoY). Analysts respond with mixed recommendations – JP Morgan’s Benny Kurniawan rates PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk overweight (target Rp 7,900), PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk neutral (target Rp 1,270) and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk underweight (target Rp 1,240); Mirae Asset’s Nafan adds PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (target Rp 7,700) and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk (target Rp 1,995); and Sucor’s Hansen recommends buying PT Mayora Indah Tbk with a lowered target of Rp 2,050.
